claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy is single-phase FCC after the specified thermomechanical processing.
The equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after the specified thermomechanical processing.
All compared alloys receive identical thermomechanical treatments.
The additional constituent in the quinary alloy alters its stacking-fault-energy landscape relative to the reduced-constituent alloys.
The altered stacking-fault-energy landscape promotes a transient FCC-to-HCP transformation during deformation.
The altered stacking-fault-energy landscape promotes deformation twinning.
Deformation-induced twinning and/or transient FCC-to-HCP transformation increases strain hardening in the quinary alloy.
Deformation-induced twinning and/or transient FCC-to-HCP transformation alters dislocation mobility in the quinary alloy.
The quaternary and ternary alloys deform primarily by dislocation glide.
The proposed dynamic processes affect deformation and failure behavior relative to the quaternary and ternary alloys.
The quinary alloy will develop a higher deformation-twin density than the quaternary and ternary alloys.
The quinary alloy will develop a higher fraction or density of transient HCP regions than the quaternary and ternary alloys.
The quinary alloy will exhibit greater strain hardening than the quaternary and ternary alloys.
The quinary alloy will exhibit higher yield strength than the quaternary and ternary alloys.
Twin and transient-HCP populations will correlate with the quinary alloy's higher yield strength and strain hardening.
In situ TEM, high-resolution EBSD, time-resolved synchrotron XRD, and high-speed imaging can be used to compare transient twinning and phase transformation among the alloys.
The comparison is restricted to identically processed, initially single-phase FCC alloys deformed under matched conditions from room to moderately elevated temperature.
Transient twinning and phase transformation may be difficult to quantify because they are subtle and time dependent.
